title: KCET 2018 Physics
subject: physics
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A

questions.q: A particle shows distance-time curve as shown in the figure [an S-shaped curve rising from P near the origin, through Q, then more steeply through R, and flattening near S at the top]. The maximum instantaneous velocity of the particle is around the point
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the distance-time graph, which is steepest around R on this curve; the KEA key accepted both P and C(R) as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of 'g' on the Earth?
options: g rises linearly to a peak at r = R then falls
g rises to a peak at r = R then falls off as a curve
g rises linearly to r = R and stays constant beyond
g stays constant up to r = R then falls off as a curve
questions.explanation: Inside the Earth g increases linearly with distance from the centre (g = g_s r/R), reaches a maximum at the surface r = R, and decreases as 1/r² outside — matching option (B).

questions.q: A cup of tea cools from 65.5°C to 62.5°C in 1 minute in a room at 22.5°C. How long will it take to cool from 46.5°C to 40.5°C in the same room?
questions.explanation: By Newton's law of cooling, (θ$_1$−θ$_2$)/t = k(θ$_{avg}$−θ$_0$). First case: 3/1 = k(64−22.5) ⟹ k = 3/41.5. Second case: 6/t = k(43.5−22.5) = k(21) ⟹ t = 6/(21×3/41.5) ≈ 4 minutes.

questions.q: The dimensions of the ratio of magnetic flux ($\phi$) and permeability ($\mu$) are
A mass 'm' on the surface of the Earth is shifted to a target equal to the radius of the Earth. If 'R' is the radius and 'M' is the mass of the Earth, then work done in this process is
questions.explanation: Work done to move a mass from the Earth's surface (r = R) to r = 2R is W = GMm(1/R − 1/2R) = GMm/2R = mgR/2, since g = GM/R².

questions.q: First overtone frequency of a closed pipe of length '$l_1$' is equal to the 2$^{nd}$ harmonic frequency of an open pipe of length '$l_2$'. The ratio $\dfrac{l_1}{l_2}$ =
questions.explanation: First overtone of closed pipe = 3v/4$l_1$; 2nd harmonic of open pipe = 2v/2$l_2$ = v/$l_2$. Equating: 3v/4$l_1$ = v/$l_2$ ⟹ $l_1$/$l_2$ = 3/4.

questions.q: The resistance R = V/I where V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. The percentage error in R is
questions.explanation: Percentage error in R = percentage error in V + percentage error in I = 5% + 2% = 7%.

questions.q: A block rests on a rough inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is 0.8. If the frictional force on the block is 10 N, the mass of the block is (g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Since the block is at rest (equilibrium), friction balances the component of weight along the incline: f = mg sin30°. So 10 = m(10)(0.5) ⟹ m = 2 kg.

questions.q: Two particles of masses m$_1$ and m$_2$ have equal kinetic energies. The ratio of their momenta is
questions.explanation: Since KE = p²/2m for equal KE, p ∝ $\sqrt{m}$, so p$_1$ : p$_2$ = $\sqrt{m_1}$ : $\sqrt{m_2}$.

questions.q: The pressure at the bottom of a liquid tank is not proportional to the
questions.explanation: Pressure at the bottom, P = h$\rho$g, depends on height, density and g, but is independent of the surface area of the liquid.

questions.q: A Carnot engine takes 300 calories of heat from a source at 500 K and rejects 150 calories of heat to the sink. The temperature of the sink is
Pressure of an ideal gas is increased by keeping temperature constant. The kinetic energy of molecules
options: Increases or decreases depending on the nature of gas
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of gas molecules depends only on the absolute temperature; since T is constant, KE remains unchanged.

questions.q: A man weighing 60 kg is in a lift moving down with an acceleration of 1.8 ms$^{-2}$. The force exerted by the floor on him is

Moment of inertia of a body about two perpendicular axes X and Y in the plane of lamina are 20 kg m² and 25 kg m² respectively. Its moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the lamina and passing through the point of intersection of X and Y axes is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: By the perpendicular axis theorem, I$_z$ = I$_x$ + I$_y$ = 20 + 25 = 45 kg m².

questions.q: Two wires A and B are stretched by the same load. If the area of cross-section of wire 'A' is double that of 'B', then the stress on 'B' is
questions.explanation: Stress = F/A for the same load F. Since A$_A$ = 2A$_B$, stress on B = F/A$_B$ = 2(F/A$_A$) = twice the stress on A.

questions.q: The magnitude of point charge due to which the electric field 30 cm away has the magnitude 2 NC$^{-1}$ will be
A mass of 1 kg carrying a charge of 2 C is accelerated through a potential of 1 V. The velocity acquired by it is

The force of repulsion between two identical positive charges when kept with a separation 'r' in air is 'F'. Half the gap between the two charges is filled by a dielectric slab of dielectric constant = 4. Then the new force of repulsion between those two charges becomes
questions.explanation: With half the gap (thickness r/2) filled by a dielectric of constant k = 4, the effective separation becomes r/2 + (r/2)$\sqrt{k}$ = r/2 + r = 3r/2, so the new force is F/(3/2)² = 4F/9.

questions.q: For the arrangement of capacitors as shown in the circuit, the effective capacitance between the points A and B is (capacitance of each capacitor is 4 $\mu$F)
questions.explanation: The KEA key gives option A, 4 $\mu$F.
questions.note: By direct circuit analysis: A is wired directly to both the top-left and bottom-left corners, so the top 4$\mu$F (A to B) and bottom 4$\mu$F (A to B) are in parallel, giving 8 $\mu$F between A and B; the remaining two 4$\mu$F capacitors plus the rightmost 4$\mu$F form a triangle hanging off B with no other external connection, so by symmetry they carry no charge and don't affect the result. This computation gives 8 $\mu$F (option D), not 4 $\mu$F, but KEA's official answer is option A.

questions.q: The work done to move a charge on an equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: Since all points on an equipotential surface are at the same potential, the potential difference is zero, so the work done in moving a charge on it is zero.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 3 $\mu$F and 6 $\mu$F are connected in series and a potential difference of 900 V is applied across the combination. They are then disconnected and reconnected in parallel. The potential difference across the combination is
questions.explanation: In series, charge Q = C$_{series}$V = 2 × 900 = 1800 $\mu$C on each capacitor. Reconnecting in parallel: if the like-charged plates are joined, V = (Q+Q)/(C$_1$+C$_2$) = 3600/9 = 400 V, but if the oppositely-charged plates are joined the charges cancel giving 0 V; the KEA key accepted both 0 V and 400 V (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Ohm's Law is applicable to
questions.explanation: Ohm's law (V = IR with constant R) holds for metallic conductors at constant temperature, not for non-ohmic devices like diodes, transistors or electrolytes.

questions.q: If the last band on the carbon resistor is absent, then the tolerance is
questions.explanation: By the resistor colour code convention, an absent tolerance band indicates a tolerance of 20%.

questions.q: The effective resistance between P and Q for the following network is [a triangle with R at the top vertex, 3$\Omega$ resistors from R to two mid-nodes, a 6$\Omega$ resistor connecting the two mid-nodes, and 4$\Omega$ and 5$\Omega$ resistors from the mid-nodes down to P and Q respectively]
questions.explanation: Converting the upper delta (3$\Omega$, 3$\Omega$, 6$\Omega$) to a star and combining in series with the 4$\Omega$ and 5$\Omega$ arms gives a net resistance between P and Q of 12 $\Omega$.

questions.q: Five identical resistors each of resistance R = 1500 $\Omega$ are connected to a 300 V battery as shown in the circuit. The reading of the ideal ammeter A is
questions.explanation: Analysing the network of five parallel-branch 1500 $\Omega$ resistors with the ammeter placed as shown, the current recorded by the ideal ammeter works out to 3/5 A.

questions.q: Two cells of internal resistances r$_1$ and r$_2$ and of same emf are connected in series, across a resistor of resistance R. If the terminal potential difference across the cells of internal resistance r$_1$ is zero, then the value of R is
questions.explanation: Terminal p.d. across cell 1 is zero means the current I satisfies I·r$_1$ = emf, i.e. I = emf/r$_1$. Total current I = 2·emf/(r$_1$+r$_2$+R). Equating gives R = r$_1$ − r$_2$.

questions.q: The I–V graphs for two different electrical appliances P and Q are shown in the diagram. If R$_P$ and R$_Q$ be the resistances of the devices, then
questions.explanation: Resistance is the reciprocal of the slope of the I–V graph; since Q has a steeper slope (larger I/V) than P, Q has lower resistance, so R$_P$ > R$_Q$.

questions.q: The correct Biot-Savart law in vector form is
questions.explanation: Using the position vector $\vec{r}$ (not the unit vector), the Biot-Savart law is d$\vec{B}$ = ($\mu_0$/4$\pi$) I(d$\vec{l}$ × $\vec{r}$)/r³.

questions.q: An electron is moving in a circle of radius r in a uniform magnetic field B. Suddenly the field is reduced to B/2. The radius of the circular path now becomes
questions.explanation: Since r = mv/(qB) and speed v is unchanged, r ∝ 1/B; halving B doubles the radius to 2r.

questions.q: A charge q is accelerated through a potential difference V. It is then passed normally through a uniform magnetic field, where it moves in a circle of radius r. The potential difference required to move it in a circle of radius 2r is
questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB) with v = $\sqrt{2qV/m}$, so r ∝ $\sqrt{V}$. To double r, V must be increased 4 times, i.e. 4V.

questions.q: A cyclotron's oscillator frequency is 10 MHz and the operating magnetic field is 0.66 T. If the radius of its dees is 60 cm, then the kinetic energy of the proton beam produced by the accelerator is
Needles N$_1$, N$_2$ and N$_3$ are made of a ferromagnetic, a paramagnetic and a diamagnetic substance respectively. A magnet when brought close to them will
options: Attract N$_1$ strongly, N$_2$ weakly and repel N$_3$ weakly
Attract N$_1$ strongly but repel N$_2$ and N$_3$ weakly
Attract N$_1$ and N$_2$ strongly but repel N$_3$
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted, paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted, and diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnet.

questions.q: The strength of the Earth's magnetic field is
options: Varying from place to place on the Earth's surface
questions.explanation: The Earth's magnetic field strength and direction vary from place to place on its surface, as described by elements like declination and dip.

questions.q: A jet plane having a wing-span of 25 m is travelling horizontally towards east with a speed of 3600 km/hour. If the Earth's magnetic field at the location is 4 × 10$^{-4}$ T and the angle of dip is 30°, then, the potential difference between the ends of the wing is
questions.explanation: The vertical component of B is B$_v$ = B sin30° = 2×10$^{-4}$ T. Speed v = 3600 km/h = 1000 m/s. emf = B$_v$·v·l = 2×10$^{-4}$×1000×25 = 5 V.

questions.q: Which of the following, represents the variation of inductive reactance (X$_L$) with the frequency of voltage source ($\nu$)?
options: A straight line through the origin rising with $\nu$
A curve starting flat near the origin and curving increasingly steeply upward as $\nu$ increases
A curve rising steeply from near the origin and then flattening as $\nu$ increases
A curve falling from a high value with $\nu$
questions.explanation: X$_L$ = 2$\pi\nu$L is directly proportional to frequency, so it is represented by a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil varies as $\phi$ = 3t² + 4t + 9. The magnitude of the emf induced at t = 2 seconds is
A 100 W bulb is connected to an AC source of 220 V, 50 Hz. Then the current flowing through the bulb is
In the series LCR circuit, the power dissipation is through
questions.explanation: In an ideal series LCR circuit, only the resistor R dissipates power; the ideal inductor and capacitor do not dissipate energy on average.

questions.q: In Karnataka, the normal domestic power supply AC is 220 V, 50 Hz. Here 220 V and 50 Hz refer to
options: Peak value of voltage and frequency
rms value of voltage and frequency
Mean value of voltage and frequency
Peak value of voltage and angular frequency
questions.explanation: The voltage and frequency ratings quoted for AC mains are conventionally the rms value of voltage and the frequency.

questions.q: A step-up transformer operates on a 230 V line and a load current of 2 A. The ratio of primary and secondary windings is 1 : 25. Then the current in the primary is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, I$_p$N$_p$ = I$_s$N$_s$ ⟹ I$_p$ = I$_s$(N$_s$/N$_p$) = 2 × 25 = 50 A.

questions.q: The number of photons falling per second on a completely darkened plate to produce a force of 6.62 × 10$^{-5}$ N is 'n'. If the wavelength of the light falling is 5 × 10$^{-7}$ m, then n = ____ × 10$^{22}$. (h = 6.62 × 10$^{-34}$ J-s)
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: Force F = n(h/$\lambda$) since the plate absorbs all photons; n = F$\lambda$/h = (6.62×10$^{-5}$ × 5×10$^{-7}$)/(6.62×10$^{-34}$) = 5×10$^{22}$.

questions.q: An object is placed at the principal focus of a convex mirror. The image will be at
questions.explanation: The KEA key gives option D, 'no image will be formed', reasoning that a convex mirror's principal focus is a virtual point behind the mirror, so a real object cannot actually be placed there.
questions.note: Applying the mirror formula formally with u = −f (f positive for a convex mirror) gives v = +f/2, an ordinary virtual image, not 'no image'; some textbooks instead read the question as a virtual object converging toward the focus, which would produce parallel reflected rays and an image at infinity (option C). The question is a known ambiguous one; KEA's official answer is D.

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the pole of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The distance of the image formed is
A candle placed 25 cm from a lens forms an image on a screen placed 75 cm on the other side of the lens. The focal length and type of the lens should be
questions.explanation: With u = −25 cm and v = +75 cm, 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/75 + 1/25 = 4/75, so f = 18.75 cm (positive, hence a convex lens).

questions.q: A plane wavefront of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a single slit of width a. The angular width of principal maximum is
questions.explanation: The central maximum in single-slit diffraction extends between the first minima on either side, at angles ±$\lambda$/a, giving a total angular width of 2$\lambda$/a.

questions.q: In a Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit, if yellow light illuminating the slit is replaced by blue light, then diffraction bands
questions.explanation: Fringe/band width in diffraction is proportional to wavelength; since blue light has a shorter wavelength than yellow, the diffraction bands become narrower.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ = 780 nm and $\lambda_2$ = 520 nm are used to obtain interference fringes. If the n$^{th}$ bright band due to $\lambda_1$ coincides with (n + 1)$^{th}$ bright band due to $\lambda_2$, then the value of n is

In Young's double slit experiment, slits are separated by 2 mm and the screen is placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. Light consisting of two wavelengths 6500 Å and 5200 Å are used to obtain interference fringes. Then the separation between the fourth bright fringes of two different patterns produced by the two wavelengths is
questions.explanation: Position of the 4th bright fringe is y = 4$\lambda$D/d. Separation = 4D($\lambda_1$−$\lambda_2$)/d = 4(1.2)(1300×10$^{-10}$)/(2×10$^{-3}$) ≈ 0.312 mm.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons depends on
options: Number of photons in the incident radiation
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: By Einstein's photoelectric equation, KE$_{max}$ = h$\nu$ − $\phi$, which depends only on the frequency of the incident radiation (for a given metal).

questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$ particle are accelerated through the same potential difference V. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths is
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: $\lambda$ = h/$\sqrt{2mqV}$, so $\lambda_p$/$\lambda_\alpha$ = $\sqrt{(m_\alpha q_\alpha)/(m_p q_p)}$ = $\sqrt{(4×2)/1}$ = $\sqrt{8}$ = 2$\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: The total energy of an electron revolving in the second orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: Total energy E$_n$ = −13.6/n² eV; for n = 2, E$_2$ = −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV.

questions.q: The period of revolution of an electron in the ground state of hydrogen atom is T. The period of revolution of the electron in the first excited state is
questions.explanation: Time period T$_n$ ∝ n³; for the first excited state n = 2, T$_2$ = 2³T = 8T.

questions.q: The energy equivalent to a substance of mass 1 g is
The half-life of tritium is 12.5 years. What mass of tritium of initial mass 64 mg will remain undecayed after 50 years?
questions.explanation: 50 years = 4 half-lives, so remaining mass = 64/2⁴ = 64/16 = 4 mg.

questions.q: In a CE amplifier, the input ac signal to be amplified is applied across
questions.explanation: In a common-emitter amplifier, the input ac signal is applied across the forward biased emitter-base junction.

questions.q: If A = 1 and B = 0, then in terms of Boolean algebra, A + $\overline{B}$ =
questions.explanation: $\overline{B}$ = 1, so A + $\overline{B}$ = 1 + 1 = 1. Since both A and $\overline{B}$ equal 1 numerically here, the KEA key accepted both option (B) $\overline{B}$ and option (C) A as correct.

questions.q: The density of an electron-hole pair in a pure germanium is 3 × 10$^{16}$ m$^{-3}$ at room temperature. On doping with aluminium, the hole density increases to 4.5 × 10$^{22}$ m$^{-3}$. Now the electron density (in m$^{-3}$) in doped germanium will be

The dc common emitter current gain of a n-p-n transistor is 50. The potential difference applied across the collector and emitter of a transistor used in CE configuration is, V$_{CE}$ = 2 V. If the collector resistance, R$_C$ = 4 k$\Omega$, the base current (I$_B$) and the collector current (I$_C$) are
questions.explanation: Since I$_C$ = $\beta$I$_B$ with $\beta$ = 50, only option (A) is self-consistent: I$_C$ = 50 × 10 $\mu$A = 500 $\mu$A = 0.5 mA.

questions.q: The radius of the Earth is 6400 km. If the height of an antenna is 500 m, then its range is
A space station is at a height equal to the radius of the Earth. If '$v_E$' is the escape velocity on the surface of the Earth, the same on the space station is ____ times $v_E$.
questions.explanation: Escape velocity at distance 2R from the centre: v' = $\sqrt{2GM/2R}$ = $\sqrt{GM/R}$ = $v_E$/$\sqrt{2}$.
